title: Automated Cleaning of Tie Point Clouds Following USGS Guidelines
author: Mohren, Schulze
materials: For example, it is suggested that a maximum of 10% of points should be removed per iteration in cleaning step 3 until a maximum tie point reprojection error within the sparse cloud of 0.3 is reached (reprojection error values are normalized by the sizes of corresponding key points). As noted by Over et al. [20], a manual iteration process by repeated filtering of 10% of the tie points remains highly time consuming. Furthermore, to achieve a timely completion of a full cleaning circle, permanent attention of the processor is required. The python script we present here aims at alleviating this iterative cleaning by automating the processing steps. Over et al. [20] also provide a detailed description of the most important quality measures for the error reconstruction procedure as provided by the software (Table 2). The list of variables (see Sect. 3.2 for more details) includes simple measures such as the unweighted root mean reprojection error of the tie points and root mean square control and check point errors, but also the number of images with less than 100 projections. steps.title: Prepare camera model
steps.instruction: Align cameras using the preferences recommended by Over et al.: set a maximum of 60 000 key points, impose no tie‑point limit per image, select high‑accuracy alignment, exclude stationary tie points, and enable self‑calibration of focal length, principal point, three radial and two tangential distortion coefficients.

steps.title: Open project and select chunk
steps.instruction: Launch the photogrammetry software, load the project, and in the graphical user interface select the chunk to be processed.

steps.title: Choose error‑reduction steps
steps.instruction: In the GUI’s filter section (panel B) tick the four tie‑point filtering steps to be applied and enable the automatic‑run option.

steps.title: Set filter parameters – step 1
steps.instruction: For Reconstruction‑uncertainty filtering set the criterion to < 50, allow a maximum of 10 %–15 % of points to be removed per iteration, and aim for a target uncertainty of 10.

steps.title: Set filter parameters – step 2
steps.instruction: For Projection‑accuracy filtering set the criterion to < 50, allow a maximum of 2 %–5 % of points to be removed per iteration, and aim for a target accuracy of 5.

steps.title: Set filter parameters – step 3
steps.instruction: For Reprojection‑error filtering set the criterion to < 0.3 (normalized by key‑point size), allow up to 10 % of points to be removed per iteration (the table lists a maximum fraction of 100 % per iteration), and stop when the maximum tie‑point reprojection error reaches 0.3.

steps.title: Set filter parameters – step 4
steps.instruction: For the final Reprojection‑error filter set the unweighted RMS reprojection error (RMSE) target to 0.13–0.18 px and use the same maximum‑fraction‑per‑iteration (up to 10 %).

steps.title: Run automated iterative cleaning
steps.instruction: Execute the provided Python script; it will iteratively apply the four filters, removing up to the specified fraction of points each pass until all target thresholds (step 1 ≤ 10, step 2 ≤ 5, step 3 ≤ 0.3, step 4 RMSE 0.13–0.18 px) are satisfied.

steps.title: Monitor quality measures
steps.instruction: After each iteration record the variables listed in Table 2: number of iterations (nI), number of tie points (nP), unweighted RMS reprojection error (RMSE), standard error per unit weight (SEUW), camera error (ecam), control‑scale error (es,co), check‑scale error (es,ch), control‑point error (ep,co), check‑point error (ep,ch), error‑reduction level (L), number of images with < 100 projections (ni<100), number of reversals (nR) and reversal points (nP,R).

steps.title: Optional optimization of steps 1‑2
steps.instruction: If desired, adjust the allowed number of iterations for step 1 and/or step 2 (the “Optimized” runs) and repeat the automated cleaning to further improve the quality measures.

steps.title: Save final results
steps.instruction: When all target thresholds are reached, save the cleaned sparse point cloud and the updated camera model for downstream processing.
